title: Basel Framework — CRE (Calculation of RWA for credit risk)
sourceNote: Structured rendering of the BCBS consolidated Basel Framework, standard group CRE (credit risk). Verbatim source: https://www.bis.org/basel_framework/standard/CRE.htm. Binds the bank via SARB Regulations Relating to Banks Reg 38.

sections.heading: Standardised approach — risk weights
sections.text: Under the standardised approach, on-balance-sheet credit exposures are assigned risk weights by counterparty class and, where available, external credit rating.

subsections.text: Exposures to sovereigns and their central banks are risk-weighted according to external rating. A national supervisor may, at its discretion, apply a lower risk weight (including 0%) to a bank's exposures to its own sovereign denominated and funded in domestic currency.

Exposures to corporates are risk-weighted between 20% and 150% according to external rating. Where no external rating is used, an investment-grade corporate exposure receives a 65% risk weight and other corporate exposures 100%.

sections.heading: Counterparty credit risk — Standardised Approach (SA-CCR)
sections.text: Counterparty credit risk for derivative transactions is measured under the Standardised Approach for measuring counterparty credit risk exposures (SA-CCR).

subsections.text: The exposure at default (EAD) for a netting set of derivative contracts is the sum of the replacement cost (RC) and the potential future exposure (PFE), scaled by a factor of 1.4: EAD = 1.4 × (RC + PFE).
